title: White-label brand configuration
description: Input to `bun run brand:apply`. Only brand.name, identifiers.bundleId, urls.website, urls.contactEmail and urls.sourceRepo are required; everything else is derived. Derived values are written back to this file so it stays a complete snapshot, but they are recomputed on every run.

name.description: Product name as shown to users, e.g. "Acme Vision". Everything else defaults from this.

shortName.description: Space-constrained form, e.g. the launcher label. Defaults to the first word of `name`.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier. Defaults to a slug of `name`. Drives the npm scope, repo name, systemd unit and R2 buckets.

legalEntity.description: Company name, used in the splash subtitle and attribution. Defaults to `name`.

bundleId.description: Reverse-DNS application id, e.g. "com.acmerobotics.vision". Becomes the Android applicationId, the iOS PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER and the Play Store id - upstream has three different values here and the rebrand collapses them to one.

kotlinPackage.description: Defaults to `bundleId` with keyword-unsafe segments escaped.

dartPackage.description: Flutter package name. Defaults to a snake_case slug. Renaming this rewrites ~940 imports.

mcapSchemaNamespace.description: Namespace for custom ROS2 schemas in recorded .mcap files. Changing it is a data-format change; see `compat.keepMcapAliases`.

driftDatabaseName.description: On-disk sqlite filename. Changing it means existing installs start with an empty database.

bookmarkKeyPrefix.description: iOS security-scoped bookmark key prefix. Changing it invalidates saved folder bookmarks.

sourceRepo.description: Your fork's repository. The in-app "view source" link points here.

playStoreAppId.description: Play Store listing id, if you have published there. Must equal identifiers.androidApplicationId - the in-app updater looks the listing up by the running app's own id. Null (the default) leaves Android update checks off.

appStoreId.description: App Store numeric id, if you have published there. Null (the default) leaves iOS update checks off.

updateFeed.description: A Sparkle-style appcast XML feed describing your releases. Takes precedence over the store ids on both platforms - use it when you ship outside the stores. Null (the default) means no feed.

reference.description: What this brand was matched against: a marketing site, a design system, a brand kit. Records nothing the engine acts on - it exists so the next run, and the next maintainer, can see that the greys were tuned to a specific reference rather than picked. Without it that reasoning evaporates the moment the conversation ends, and the next person re-derives the palette from the logo and quietly undoes the match.

url.description: The site, design system or file the tokens were read from.

capturedAt.description: ISO date the reference was read. A live site drifts; this says how stale the match may be.

notes.description: What was matched and what could not be - "accent from --color-primary, tint 0.45 for their warm off-white; their gradients and illustration have no equivalent here".

developmentTeam.description: Apple Developer team id. Left null on purpose - the engine blanks the upstream team rather than leaving your build signed against someone else's.

tint.description: How much of the accent bleeds into the neutral surfaces, borders and muted text. 0 (the default) keeps upstream's greys exactly; 1 mixes up to 14% of the accent into the page background. This is the knob that makes one hex visibly re-skin the app rather than recolour a badge. Semantic colours (red, green, blue) and the black/white anchors never take tint.

allowLowContrast.description: Ship a palette whose contrast is worse than upstream's and below WCAG AA. Off by default: a tint that walks body text below AA is a regression, and it is invisible on the screen of whoever chose the colour. Run `bun run brand:preview` to see the grades.

overrides.description: Pin any named token on class C in apps/mobile/lib/src/core/theme/colors.dart. Applied after the tint, so this is the one sanctioned place to disagree with the derivation. An unknown token name is an error - it used to generate a constant nothing read.

space.description: The spacing scale - how much air the product has. Density survives a palette swap: two apps sharing a colour, a corner radius and a typeface still read as different products when one breathes and the other is packed. Every gap and pad in the app is on this scale.

style.description: tight is roughly 0.75x upstream, comfortable roughly 1.25x, rounded to whole pixels at each step. `default` reproduces the literals already in the widget tree, so leaving this alone is a no-op on every pixel.

scale.description: Override individual steps of the chosen density, in logical pixels. The `*Plus` steps are the half-steps between the named ones, and exist because the widget tree genuinely uses 6, 10, 14, 20 and 28 - leaving them off the scale would mean those gaps stopped following the brand.

type.description: The typographic scale. `fonts.*` picks the typefaces; this decides how big they are, how tightly they are set and how heavy they run. Changing the family alone leaves a fork at upstream's exact ramp, which is the most convincing way to look rebranded without being it.

style.description: compact tightens the ramp and the leading, default is upstream, spacious opens both. Every TextStyle in the app is built from the chosen table.

scale.description: Override individual steps of the chosen style. Both measures are logical pixels; `lineHeight` is absolute, not a multiplier, and is converted to Flutter's ratio at generation. Either key may be given alone.

xl3Plus.description: The half-step the app's page titles sit on. It exists so those titles follow the brand instead of being the two headings that do not.

weights.description: The four weights the widget tree uses, by role. A reference that runs light or heavy is expressed here and reaches every label at once. Must be multiples of 100 - Flutter has no FontWeight in between, and a 550 would round to a neighbour without telling you.

shape.description: The corner-radius scale, which is most of what makes two apps look like different products rather than one app in two colours.

style.description: sharp 0-8px, soft 4-24px (upstream, the default), rounded 6-32px, pill 8-44px. Every radius in the app is on this scale, so the style reaches the whole product.

scale.description: Override individual steps of the chosen style, in logical pixels. The *Plus steps are the half-steps between the named ones.

full.description: Sentinel for "circle or stadium". Leave at 999 unless you know why you are changing it.

fonts.description: The four typeface roles. Naming a family that is neither bundled nor supplied under `files` is an error, because Flutter renders an unknown family as the system face without reporting anything.

display.description: Headlines and the splash wordmark. Default EBGaramond.

body.description: Body copy and UI labels - by far the most used. Default Geist.

accent.description: The character face, used sparingly for large display numerals. Default Handjet.

files.description: Family name -> the font files to bundle for it. Required for any family not already in apps/mobile/pubspec.yaml. Files are copied into apps/mobile/assets/fonts/ and declared in the pubspec.

oneOf.description: Repo-relative path to a .ttf or .otf, e.g. packages/brand/source/fonts/Inter.ttf

replaceBundled.description: Delete the upstream typefaces that no declared family still uses. Set true if you cannot redistribute them under your own brand.

iconSource.description: Repo-relative path to a square PNG (>=512px, 1024 preferred) or an SVG. All launcher icon densities are generated from it. Null means a placeholder monogram is used.

iconMonochrome.description: Android 13+ themed-icon layer. Derived from the foreground when absent, but hand-drawn is much better.

logoLight.description: The mark shown *inside* the app: splash screen, sign-in sheet, onboarding modal, iOS launch screen. Defaults to iconForeground, then iconSource - so supplying only an icon no longer leaves upstream's logo on those screens.

logoDark.description: Dark-mode variant. Defaults to the same artwork as logoLight, which is fine for a mark that works on both and invisible for one that does not - `bun run brand:preview` renders it on both backgrounds.

iosUsageDescriptions.description: The six permission prompts iOS shows the user. Defaults are built from the app name.

attribution.description: Credit to the upstream project. Disabling this does not remove your obligation to retain LICENSE and the upstream copyright notice.

compat.description: Choices that trade compatibility with data written by the pre-rebrand app. All three are harmless for a fresh fork and destructive for an update-in-place.

keepMcapAliases.description: Keep decoding the previous namespace's MCAP schemas, so recordings made before the rebrand still open.

legacy.description: Set by the engine, not by hand.

lineHeight.description: Absolute logical pixels, e.g. 24 for "24px on a 16px face".
